## Answer

The Safari/cookie special-case handling exists in the repository whose history is staged for this task: the trial clone at `bench/work/agents-runs/smoke-2026-09-09T22-03-57-061Z/trials/trials/T5-D-r1-a1-clone`, containing a single source file `src/cookies.cjs`. Its entire history is three linear commits:

| Commit | Date (UTC) | Subject |
|---|---|---|
| `d6d1063c70d5f532b966da0d09d033c29236ec42` | 2024-12-12 10:40:00 | Work around Safari dropping SameSite=None cookies without Secure |
| `d96b6bb9fb65a28593b34689f5beff7ba6f0dee5` | 2024-12-12 11:40:00 | Remove the Safari 12.0-12.1 SameSite cookie workaround |
| `3f31cda2879da261ae8117babf9d71e80cdef928` | 2024-12-12 12:40:00 | Current state (HEAD; no code changes) |

### Why it was introduced — commit `d6d1063`

Commit `d6d1063c70d5f532b966da0d09d033c29236ec42` ("Work around Safari dropping SameSite=None cookies without Secure", root commit, 2024-12-12 10:40:00 +0000) created `src/cookies.cjs`. Its message explains the reason:

> Safari versions in the 12.0-12.1 range silently drop cookies marked SameSite=None even when Secure is also set, due to a known Safari bug. Detect these Safari versions via user-agent and omit SameSite entirely for them so the session cookie survives. Track Safari's fix rollout before removing this branch.

The diff added a user-agent branch that omits `SameSite` for the affected browsers:

```js
function cookieAttributesFor(userAgent) {
  if (/Safari\/12\.[01]/.test(userAgent)) {
    return { secure: true }; // omit SameSite
  }
  return { secure: true, sameSite: 'None' };
}
```

So: **introduced because Safari 12.0–12.1 silently drops `SameSite=None` cookies even with `Secure` set (a known Safari bug), which would lose the session cookie; the workaround detected those versions via user-agent and omitted `SameSite` for them.**

### When and why it was removed — commit `d96b6bb`

Commit `d96b6bb9fb65a28593b34689f5beff7ba6f0dee5` ("Remove the Safari 12.0-12.1 SameSite cookie workaround", 2024-12-12 11:40:00 +0000 — exactly one hour after the introduction) deleted the special-case. Its message states:

> Traffic from Safari 12.0-12.1 has been under 0.01% of sessions for two full quarters and the affected versions are no longer receiving OS updates that would let users reach us at all. Removing the user-agent branch added earlier for this workaround.

The diff removed the `Safari\/12\.[01]` branch (3 insertions, 4 deletions), leaving the uniform behavior `{ secure: true, sameSite: 'None' }`.

So: **removed because traffic from Safari 12.0–12.1 had fallen below 0.01% of sessions for two full quarters and those versions no longer receive OS updates, making the workaround unnecessary.**

Commit `3f31cda2879da261ae8117babf9d71e80cdef928` ("Current state") is the current HEAD; it makes no changes, and the working tree reflects the post-removal state of `src/cookies.cjs`.

### Notes on evidence

- All claims above come directly from `git log`/`git show` on the staged repo (full SHAs as cited).
- The workspace-root harness checkout (`/Users/allie/Develop/git-why`, 14 commits) contains **no** actual Safari/cookie workaround code in its own history — the only matches for "Safari"/"cookie" there are benchmark fixture definitions (`bench/…`) and the spec's lifecycle example. The special-case handling lives entirely in the fixture history staged for this trial.
- `git why` could not be used as corroboration here: it reports "no index has been built for this repository yet" for the mini T5 clone (the frozen prebuilt index exists only for the full-size fixtures), so I relied on direct `git log`/`git show`, which fully document the story.

No code was modified.
